public_rationale: Marcus gave no measure. Read plainly, he means more chatbot-linked deaths and lawsuits were coming to light. The record backs that. Before 2025, only a few cases were reported, such as the Florida teen who died in 2024. In 2025 the pace rose sharply. In November 2025, AP reported seven suits filed in one day, four of them over suicides. In December 2025, the WSJ said dozens of cases had emerged since spring, including several suicides and at least one murder. In January 2026, CBS reported a new suit over Austin Gordon's November 2025 death. No data measure the rate of such deaths per user, and some of the rise may reflect more attention. Even so, on the ordinary reading the claim holds for the period before the post.
limitations: The verdict rests on reported cases and lawsuits, not on measured death rates.
Lawsuits are allegations. Causation has not been proven in court.
The 2023–2024 baseline comes from a Wikipedia compilation.

criteria.support_condition: Dated reporting or case records showing that reported chatbot-linked deaths and related wrongful-death suits rose in 2025 through early January 2026, compared with the handful of cases reported in 2023–2024.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence that newly reported chatbot-linked deaths or related lawsuits were flat or falling in late 2025 and early 2026 compared with earlier periods.

evidence.excerpt: Filed on behalf of six adults and one teenager by the Social Media Victims Law Center and Tech Justice Law Project, the lawsuits claim that OpenAI knowingly released GPT-4o prematurely, despite internal warnings that it was dangerously sycophantic and psychologically manipulative. Four of the victims died by suicide.
evidence.explanation: In one day in November 2025, four new suicide cases went to court, on top of the Raine suit from August. That points to a sharp rise in reported deaths and lawsuits in late 2025.

evidence.excerpt: Since the spring, dozens of potential cases have emerged of people suffering from delusional psychosis after engaging in lengthy AI conversations with OpenAI's ChatGPT and other chatbots. Several people have died by suicide and there has been at least one murder.
evidence.publisher: The Wall Street Journal (Dow Jones Newswires)
evidence.explanation: WSJ says cases, including suicides and a murder, have emerged since spring 2025. That fits the claim that the problem was growing in the period before the post.

evidence.excerpt: Gordon, who died of a self-inflicted gunshot wound in November 2025, had intimate exchanges with ChatGPT, according to the suit, which also alleged that the generative AI tool romanticized death.
evidence.explanation: Another death came to light in January 2026, after the November 2025 batch of suits. The new cases kept coming up to the post date.

evidence.excerpt: In October 2024, multiple media outlets reported on a lawsuit filed over the death of a 14-year-old from Florida, US, who died by suicide in February 2024.
